name: Trendione

lead: Trendione (Trenavar) is a metabolite of trenbolone that has been sold online as a prohormone-type supplement. People use it for more muscle and a harder look.

It is inactive itself in receptor assays, with more than 100-fold lower affinity than trenbolone for androgen and progesterone receptors; the idea is that the body converts it to trenbolone. Most published work on it concerns environmental fate, since trenbolone acetate is used as a cattle growth implant and trendione is excreted in manure. No human studies exist.

paras: It has been sold as an oral supplement through online channels. No standard routine or timeline is documented.
No human safety data exist. It is listed in the US Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act of 2014, so legal restrictions apply there.

angle.text: Trendione is sold as a trenbolone-type prohormone for more muscle and a harder look, on the idea that the body converts it to trenbolone and activates androgen receptors. It has been studied mostly in cattle-manure environmental work, not in people.

lead: Trendione (estra-4,9,11-triene-3,17-dione; code RU-2065; nicknamed 'Trenavar' or 'Trenevar') is a steroid that is a metabolite of the anabolic steroid trenbolone and has been sold online as a prohormone-type supplement. Users who take prohormones of this type aim for a leaner, more muscular physique, and one T Nation member described a 'shredded' look after using it.[1][2]

The proposed chain is that the body converts a precursor into the active steroid, in the way androstenedione relates to testosterone; Wikipedia draws this comparison.[1] In receptor assays trendione itself binds androgen and progesterone receptors more than 100-fold less strongly than trenbolone.[1][3]

Most published work on it concerns environmental fate: trenbolone acetate is used as a cattle growth implant, and trendione is excreted in manure and studied in soil and runoff.[4][5] It is listed in the US Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act of 2014.[1] No human trials of trendione have been published.

Trenbolone itself, the parent compound, was first synthesised in 1963, has veterinary use as a cattle growth implant and was never approved for human use; it is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US [6]. Trendione's role in that story is as one of its metabolites, which is why researchers studying cattle manure and runoff measure it alongside 17-alpha and 17-beta trenbolone [4][5].
infobox: Listed in the 2014 Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act[1]

paras: Wikipedia classes trendione as an androgen, anabolic steroid and progestogen prohormone and describes it as inactive itself, with affinity for the androgen and progesterone receptors more than 100-fold lower than trenbolone.[1] A receptor study found the affinity of the major trenbolone metabolites, including trendione, was under 5 percent of that of 17beta-trenbolone.[3]

In humans given labelled 17-beta-trenbolone as a tracer, 54 percent of the radioactivity appeared in urine within 26 hours and 63 percent within 72 hours; more than half of the urinary material was glucuronide conjugates containing mainly 17-alpha-trenbolone, 17-beta-trenbolone and trendione [7]. The authors noted that disposition in humans differs significantly from that in rats [7]. Wikipedia's trenbolone article says that studies disagree about whether trenbolone is converted by aromatase or 5-alpha-reductase, and that the popular claim that it is five times as potent as testosterone is not established, with rat studies suggesting roughly three to five times [6].

Wikipedia describes trendione as being to trenbolone what androstenedione is to testosterone: a prohormone that is itself largely inactive and would need to be converted in the body to act [1]. How efficiently, or whether, this conversion happens after oral intake by people has not been reported.

Wikipedia describes it as a designer steroid sold online as a dietary supplement.[1] On T Nation, a poster listing past anabolic use said low-dose 'trenevar' in 2015 helped them get very lean.[2] Another thread asks how long trendione and related products remain traceable in the body.[8]
The same Wikipedia article cites a 2016 Military Medicine case report of acute pancreatitis linked to a supplement containing anabolic-androgenic steroids.[1]

Trenbolone's own history includes veterinary use in cattle and a human clinical ester that is no longer marketed, according to Wikipedia; sport authorities list doping cases involving the parent drug [6]. Trendione-type products are sold as prohormone supplements marketed under names such as Trenavar, and the product is named in the US 2014 Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act [1].
Trendione is named in the US Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act of 2014.[1]

Trenbolone acetate has been used as a growth promoter in US beef cattle since 1987 [9]. Studies of implanted cattle identify 17-alpha-trenbolone and trendione as the main metabolites in manure. In a mass-balance study of manure from cattle implanted with 40 mg of trenbolone acetate and 8 mg of estradiol, a maximum of 9.3 percent of the implant dose was excreted as 17-alpha-trenbolone over 113 days, and under 1 percent as 17-beta-trenbolone or trendione [10]. Research has examined how they degrade in agricultural soils, sorb to soil and break down under light [4][5].

In aerobic water microcosms dosed with about 1,400 ng/L of the metabolites, observed half-lives at 20 C were about 0.9 days for 17-beta-trenbolone, 1.3 days for trendione and 2.2 days for 17-alpha-trenbolone, with longer half-lives in colder conditions [11]. In a 14-day study, adult female medaka fish exposed to the metabolites showed changes in ovarian follicles, and trendione reduced whole-body estradiol and testosterone [9]. A study of a Midwest tile-drained farm receiving animal waste measured hormone discharge to the receiving drainage [12].

No studies found of trendione in people as a supplement or drug. The published literature consists of receptor-binding assays [3], one human tracer study of its parent compound that detected trendione as a urinary metabolite [7], and environmental and animal studies [4][5][9][10][11].

lore.intro: On T Nation, trendione appears in threads on prohormones, recomposition and drug-test detection windows.[2][8]
